title: Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff as Susie Wiles exits after midterm loss
dek: Miller, architect of the administration's immigration crackdown, takes over on Monday. Wiles moves to Trump's political operation.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hard-line immigration and deportation policies, as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles three days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.

Mr Trump announced the change on Truth Social on Friday, US time, saying Mr Miller, "one of my most trusted advisors", would take over on Monday, 9 November. He said Ms Wiles, "who has done an outstanding job", would move to his political operation. Ms Wiles, who gave Mr Trump her resignation on Thursday night according to reports, wrote on X that Friday was her last day and that serving in the White House "has been the honor of a lifetime". Neither gave a reason for her departure.

Ms Wiles, 69, was the first woman to hold the post and Mr Trump's longest-serving chief of staff; he had four in his first term. She ran his 2016 Florida campaign and his 2020 and 2024 campaigns. Mr Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, joined Mr Trump's 2016 campaign as a speechwriter after working for Senator Jeff Sessions.

The appointment puts the official most closely identified with Mr Trump's immigration crackdown in charge of the White House as it faces a Democratic Congress, and as the president weighs whether to resume large-scale strikes on Iran. For India, Mr Miller's influence matters chiefly through US immigration policy, including work visas used by many Indian professionals.
